title: Characteristics of physical and chemical changes
competency: Distinguish physical and chemical changes using their characteristics.

keywords.def: A change in physical appearance, not in chemical composition. No new substance forms.
A change in chemical composition. New substances form.

ideas.name: How to tell the two changes apart

en.text: A physical change forms no new substance, keeps the composition, is easily reversed and need not involve energy changes. A chemical change forms new substances with new properties, alters the composition, comes with energy changes and is not easily reversed.

screens.title: Can it go back?
screens.ask: Ice melts and can freeze again. Can ash turn back into wood?
screens.after:
No. Ash cannot become wood again.
Burning made new substances: ash, smoke and gases.
Chemical changes are not easily reversed. Physical changes, like melting ice, usually are.

screens.title: 2.4.3 Characteristics of physical and chemical changes
table: New substances with new properties form
A change in a physical property
A change in a chemical property

screens.title: Physical or chemical change? Tap each part.
sets: No new substance. Composition not altered. Easily reversed by physical means. Energy changes not necessary. Example: melting ice.
New substances with new properties. Composition altered. Not easily reversed. Accompanied by energy changes. Example: burning wood.
overlaps: Both are changes in matter. Both happen around us all the time.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A change in physical appearance, not in chemical composition. No new substance forms.
A change in chemical composition. New substances form.

screens.text: Which is a characteristic of a chemical change?
opts: New substances with new properties form
screens.ans: New substances with new properties form
screens.why:
In a chemical change new substances form.
The new substances have new properties.
"Easily reversed", "composition stays the same" and "only shape changes" describe a physical change.

items: Nothing new forms in a physical change.
Burning gives out heat and light: an energy change.
Ice melts and freezes back easily.
New substances mean a new composition.
Size, shape or state change, but not composition.
screens.why:
Physical change: no new substance, easily reversed, a change in a physical property.
Chemical change: composition altered, not easily reversed, accompanied by energy changes.
These are the two lists on page 50.
screens.text: Sort each characteristic: does it describe a physical change or a chemical change?
Check three statements about physical changes. I: easily reversible. II: no new substance. III: no change in mass. Which are correct?
screens.why:
I: true. Melted ice can be frozen again.
II: true. A physical change never forms a new substance.
III: true. The amount of matter stays the same; only its appearance changes.
So I, II and III are all correct.

screens.text: Physical or chemical? Chala boils an egg. It becomes solid and cannot be made raw again. Which change is it, and why?
opts: Physical, because only the state changes
Chemical, because a new substance forms and it cannot be reversed
screens.ans: Chemical, because a new substance forms and it cannot be reversed
screens.why:
Heating changes the egg into a new substance: cooked egg.
It cannot be turned back into a raw egg.
A new substance and not reversible → chemical change.
It is not just a change of state, like melting ice.
screens.clue: Can you turn a boiled egg back into a raw one?

test.text: True or false? A chemical change is easily reversed.
test.why:
A chemical change makes new substances.
They cannot easily be turned back. Ash does not become wood again.
So the statement is false.

test.text: What happens to composition? In a physical change, the composition of the substance …
test.why:
A physical change alters only appearance: size, shape or state.
What the substance is made of stays the same.
So the composition is not altered.

test.text: Which sign shows a chemical change?
opts: A new substance with new properties
test.ans: A new substance with new properties
test.why:
Shape and size changes are physical.
Dissolving is physical too: the solid can be recovered.
A new substance with new properties is the sign of a chemical change.

test.text: True or false? Chemical changes are accompanied by energy changes.
test.why:
A burning candle gives out heat and light.
Heat and light are forms of energy.
The book says chemical changes are accompanied by energy changes. True.

test.text: Physical or chemical? Which statement is correct?
opts: Digestion of food is a chemical change
Burning paper is a physical change
test.ans: Digestion of food is a chemical change
test.why:
Evaporation only changes water to vapour: physical, so the first is wrong.
Burning paper forms ash and gases: chemical, so the third is wrong.
Digestion breaks food into new, simpler substances: chemical.
So only "digestion of food is a chemical change" is correct.
